# NRRF788 — QM has no classical foundation, QG is translational truth; prime holes, type-class equivalence, set uniqueness

Machine-checked module: `NRRF788QMNotClassicalQGTranslationalTruthPrimeHoleSetUniqueness.lean`
(registered in `lakefile.toml`; builds with no `sorry` and a machine-checked axiom audit).

## The question

> Prime topology hole type class equivalence. Set uniqueness. For physics classical object operator
> foundations: those physical derivations are all included within a third translation of my specific
> natural forms into the quantum gravity closure. The problem is that QM is not a classical theory
> with classical foundations, and QG is not a non-classical foundation, it is translational truth.

## The setting

Everything is carried by the loop sensor: a reading of the translation line `ℤ` into a loop of
period `k`, advancing one step per translation.

* A **classical object/operator foundation** at resolution `k` is exactly what the classical picture
  demands: absolute values assigned to the sites (the objects), a translation operator acting on
  them by one step per translation, and the requirement that those values *reproduce* the sensor's
  verdicts.
* The **quantum phase** at resolution `k` is one loop reading.
* The **third translation** of the natural forms into the quantum-gravity closure is the whole
  family of loop readings at once — and, sharpened, its prime sub-family.

## What the module proves

**1. QM is not a classical theory with classical foundations.**
At every looping resolution `k ≥ 1` there is *no* classical object/operator foundation at all — the
type of such foundations is empty. Absolute values transported by a translation operator cannot
reproduce even a single loop reading, because the loop identifies `0` with `k` while the operator
insists they differ by `k`. Moreover a classical foundation exists **exactly** when `k = 0`: the
classical case is the degenerate, loopless case of the sensor, not the ground beneath it.

**2. QG is not a "non-classical foundation": it is translational truth.**
No single relative reading is the truth — at every looping resolution distinct translations read
alike. But the *totality* of the relative readings is faithful: two translations read alike by every
looping sensor are the same translation, and the unique admissible sheaf relation of that
quantum-gravity reading is equality itself. Truth is the absolute translation of all the relative
readings; nothing is placed underneath them.

**3. Prime topology holes, type-class equivalence, set uniqueness.**
Every *finite* family of resolutions leaves a **hole**: a nonzero translation that every sensor of
the family reads as no translation at all (their product). So no finite set of relative readings
closes. The prime family closes it exactly: a translation divisible by every prime is zero, hence
the prime classes of a translation determine it, and the set of translations carrying a given system
of prime classes is a **singleton** — set uniqueness. Equivalently, the type-class equivalence
generated by all primes is equality.

**4. The third translation contains the physical derivations.**
Each fixed-resolution reading — the setting in which classical-operator style derivations are
carried out — is literally a *component* of the third translation, and the third translation is
strictly finer than every one of its components. So the physical derivations are all included within
it, while none of them is it.

A single summary theorem collects (1)–(4).

## Caveats

The "classical foundation" formalized here is the specific structure described above (absolute
site-values, operator acting by translation, reproducing the sensor's verdicts). The impossibility
theorem is a theorem about that structure and the loop sensor, not about the whole of physics; what
it shows precisely is that this classical ground cannot underwrite even one loop reading, whereas
the family of all such readings is faithful.
